instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a passage or table; the set stays together.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: According to the National Forest Policy, what share of India's geographical area should ideally be under forest?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) One-third
Why: NCERT notes that the National Forest Policy aims for one-third, or about 33 per cent, of the geographical area to be under forest.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not the policy target.
Key point: The actual forest area is well below this target.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, what is household or cottage manufacturing?
options: A) Large factories with assembly lines run by big companies
B) High-tech units in science parks near major universities
C) Artisans making goods at home with local materials and tools
D) Mines and quarries that extract raw materials for export
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Artisans making goods at home with local materials and tools
Why: NCERT describes household or cottage manufacturing as the smallest unit, where artisans use local raw materials and simple tools to make everyday goods at home, with family members or part-time labour.
Why not the others: (A) is large-scale manufacturing; (B) is high-tech industry; (D) is a primary activity.
Key point: Pottery and handicrafts are typical cottage products.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: According to NCERT, about 71 per cent of the earth's surface is covered with water. What share of the total water is fresh water?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) About 3 per cent
Why: NCERT notes that water is a cyclic resource with abundant supplies, but fresh water makes up only about 3 per cent of the total.
Why not the others: About 71 per cent (D) is the share of the surface covered by water; (A) and (C) are not NCERT figures.
Key point: Fresh water is limited and unevenly distributed.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: What does the warabandi system, followed in the Indira Gandhi Canal command area, mean?
options: A) A ban on all farming in the canal area
B) Equal sharing of canal water within an outlet's command area
C) Giving all the water to the largest landholders first
D) Selling canal water to industries in towns
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Equal sharing of canal water within an outlet's command area
Why: NCERT describes warabandi as the equal distribution of canal water in the command area of an outlet.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not what the term means.
Key point: Strict water management is needed to prevent waterlogging and salinity.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Mineral belt)
(A) North-eastern plateau region
(B) South-western plateau region
(C) North-western region
(D) Himalayan belt

List-II (Minerals in NCERT)
(I) Copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten
(II) Copper and zinc, along the Aravalli, with building stones
(III) High-grade iron ore, manganese and limestone, but little coal
(IV) Iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica, in the Chotanagpur area
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: the north-eastern plateau, including Chotanagpur, has iron ore, coal, manganese, bauxite and mica (IV); the south-western plateau has high-grade iron ore, manganese and limestone, but no coal except Neyveli lignite (III); the north-western region, along the Aravalli, has copper and zinc and building stones (II); the Himalayan belt has copper, lead, zinc, cobalt and tungsten (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the two plateau regions; (B) swaps the south-western and north-western regions; (C) swaps the north-western region and the Himalayan belt.
Key point: Most minerals occur in the old crystalline rocks of the peninsula.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question:
Arrange the following coalfields of the Damodar valley from west to east:
(A) Karanpura
(B) Raniganj
(C) Jharia
(D) Bokaro
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (D), (C), (B)
Why: Karanpura lies furthest upstream in the west (A), followed by Bokaro (D) and Jharia (C), with Raniganj in West Bengal furthest east (B).
Why not the others: (B) puts Bokaro west of Karanpura; (C) puts Jharia west of Bokaro; (D) puts Raniganj west of Jharia.
Key point: Jharia is the largest coalfield, followed by Raniganj.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, why does mining matter so much to many developing countries of Africa, South America and Asia?
options: A) More than half of their earnings come from minerals alone
B) They have stopped all other economic activities
C) Mining needs no capital or technology in these countries
D) Their mines produce only for their own home markets
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) More than half of their earnings come from minerals alone
Why: NCERT notes that many developing nations of Africa, and a few of South America and Asia, earn over half of their income from minerals alone.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are false.
Key point: In developed economies, high labour costs have pushed some mining away.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, how is population growth generally related to the level of economic development?
options: A) Negatively — developed countries usually grow more slowly
B) Positively — richer countries always grow the fastest
C) Not at all — every country grows at the same rate
D) Only in Africa, and nowhere else in the world
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Negatively — developed countries usually grow more slowly
Why: NCERT notes a negative correlation between economic development and population growth: developed countries generally grow slowly, while many developing countries grow fast.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) contradict NCERT.
Key point: Population change reflects a country's economic development and social uplift.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: From where does the Indira Gandhi Canal originate?
options: A) The Bhakra dam in Himachal Pradesh
B) The Hirakud dam in Odisha
C) The Farakka barrage in West Bengal
D) The Harike barrage in Punjab
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The Harike barrage in Punjab
Why: NCERT notes that the canal originates at the Harike barrage in Punjab and runs parallel to the Pakistan border.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are other water projects, not the canal's source.
Key point: The canal carries water into the Thar Desert.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question: Country X has an HDI value of 0.912 and Country Y has a value of 0.645. By how much does X's value exceed Y's?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 0.267
Given: HDI of X = 0.912; HDI of Y = 0.645.
Step 1: Gap = 0.912 − 0.645.
Step 2: = 0.267.
Common mistake: adding the two values (1.557, option A), or dividing them (about 1.414, option D).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question: How does knowledge processing outsourcing (KPO) differ from business process outsourcing (BPO), according to NCERT?
options: A) KPO uses unskilled workers only, for routine data entry
B) KPO deals only with manufacturing goods in factories
C) It uses highly skilled workers for knowledge work such as research
D) KPO is carried on only inside government offices and nowhere else
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) It uses highly skilled workers for knowledge work such as research
Why: NCERT notes that KPO involves highly skilled workers doing information-driven work, such as research and development, e-learning, business research and legal services.
Why not the others: (A) is closer to BPO; (B) and (D) are false.
Key point: KPO helps companies create additional business opportunities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
An oil pipeline runs from Salaya in Gujarat to Jalandhar in Punjab. Arrange the following places along it from Salaya to Jalandhar:
(A) Jalandhar
(B) Mathura
(C) Viramgam
(D) Salaya
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (D), (C), (B), (A)
Why: NCERT notes that the pipeline runs from Salaya (D) via Viramgam (C), Mathura (B), Delhi and Sonipat to Jalandhar (A).
Why not the others: (A) puts Mathura before Viramgam; (B) starts at Viramgam; (D) puts Jalandhar before Mathura.
Key point: Pipelines are the most convenient way to carry liquids and gases over long distances.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, which industries use non-metallic minerals as their raw material?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Cement and pottery
Why: NCERT notes that some mineral-based industries use non-metallic minerals, as in the cement and pottery industries.
Why not the others: Iron and steel (A) use ferrous minerals; copper and aluminium (B) are non-ferrous metals; leather and wool (C) are animal-based.
Key point: Mineral-based industries may use ferrous, non-ferrous or non-metallic minerals.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: According to NCERT, on what basis is pollution classified into air, water, land and noise pollution?
options: A) The country in which it was first observed
B) The time of day at which it occurs
C) The colour of the pollutant
D) The medium through which pollutants spread
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The medium through which pollutants spread
Why: NCERT classifies pollution by the medium through which pollutants are transported and diffused — air, water, land and noise.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the basis NCERT uses.
Key point: Pollution results from the release of substances and energy from human activities.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: A region's population rose from 50 lakh to 56 lakh in ten years. What was its percentage growth over the decade?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 12 per cent
Given: earlier population = 50 lakh; later population = 56 lakh.
Step 1: Increase = 56 − 50 = 6 lakh.
Step 2: Growth = 6 ÷ 50 × 100 = 12 per cent.
Common mistake: giving the increase in lakh as a percentage (6, option A), or dividing by the later population (about 10.7 per cent, option B).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about world population, according to NCERT:
(A) About 90 per cent of the world's people live in about 10 per cent of its land area.
(B) The ten most populous countries hold about 60 per cent of the world's population.
(C) Six of these ten countries are in Asia.
(D) It took about 500 years for the world's population to rise from 5 billion to 6 billion.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — the rise from 5 billion to 6 billion took only about 12 years. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Population is very unevenly distributed across the world.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Ganga plains are among the most densely populated areas of the world.
Reason (R): Mountains and hills are better suited than plains to farming, roads and industries.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: The Assertion is true. The Reason is false — NCERT notes that flat plains and gentle slopes, not mountains, favour crops, roads and industries, while hilly areas hinder transport.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) need a true Reason; (D) needs a false Assertion.
Key point: The Andes, Alps and Himalaya are thinly populated.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Farming system)
(A) Mediterranean agriculture
(B) Market gardening and horticulture
(C) Extensive commercial grain cultivation
(D) Dairy farming

List-II (Speciality in NCERT)
(I) Milk and milk products for urban and industrial centres
(II) Wheat, the principal crop
(III) Tulips, flown to cities across Europe from the Netherlands
(IV) Viticulture, or grapes grown for wine
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: viticulture is a speciality of the Mediterranean region (IV); the Netherlands grows tulips for markets across Europe (III); wheat is the principal crop of extensive grain farms (II); dairy farms supply milk and milk products to cities (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Mediterranean farming and horticulture; (B) swaps horticulture and grain; (D) swaps grain and dairy.
Key point: Each farming system specialises according to climate and market.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Which canals connect the Great Lakes of North America to form an inland waterway, according to NCERT?
options: A) The Soo Canal and the Welland Canal
B) The Suez Canal and the Panama Canal
C) The Kiel Canal and the Volga–Don Canal
D) The Buckingham Canal and the Indira Gandhi Canal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Soo Canal and the Welland Canal
Why: NCERT notes that Lakes Superior, Huron, Erie and Ontario are connected by the Soo Canal and the Welland Canal to form an inland waterway.
Why not the others: (B) are inter-ocean canals; (C) are in Europe; (D) are in India.
Key point: Duluth and Buffalo are major ports on this waterway.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about approaches to human geography:
(A) The welfare or humanistic school was concerned with social well-being, such as housing, health and education.
(B) The radical school used Marxian theory to explain poverty, deprivation and social inequality.
(C) The behavioural school stressed lived experience and the perception of space by social groups.
(D) The quantitative revolution was concerned mainly with lived experience and perception.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — the quantitative revolution relied on statistical tools to make geography more scientific. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Post-modernism, in the 1990s, questioned grand generalisations.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about intensive subsistence agriculture dominated by wet paddy:
(A) It is found largely in the densely populated regions of monsoon Asia.
(B) Land holdings are very small because of the high density of population.
(C) Farmers use family labour, which leads to intensive use of the land.
(D) Farmers use large machinery on huge farms.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — NCERT notes that the use of machinery is limited and most operations are done by hand. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Farmyard manure is used to keep the soil fertile.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, physiological density is the total population divided by:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The net cultivated area
Why: NCERT defines physiological density as the total population divided by the net cultivated area.
Why not the others: (A) gives arithmetic density; (C) and (D) are not used in this measure.
Key point: It shows the pressure of population on farmland.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: According to NCERT, which body was formed in 1948 by some countries to free world trade from high customs tariffs?
options: A) The United Nations Development Programme
D) The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
Why: NCERT notes that in 1948, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) was formed to liberalise trade from high tariffs and other restrictions.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the body formed for this purpose.
Key point: GATT was transformed into the WTO in 1995.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: According to NCERT, national highways form only about 2 per cent of India's total road length. About what share of road traffic do they carry?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) About 40 per cent
Why: NCERT notes that national highways make up only about 2 per cent of road length but carry about 40 per cent of road traffic.
Why not the others: (B) is their share of road length; (C) and (D) are not NCERT figures.
Key point: National highways are built and maintained by the central government.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: If the value of a country's imports is more than the value of its exports, its balance of trade is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Negative, or unfavourable
Why: NCERT notes that if imports exceed exports, the country has a negative or unfavourable balance of trade.
Why not the others: (B) is the case when exports exceed imports; (C) and (D) are false.
Key point: Balance of trade records the volume of goods and services exported and imported.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: Which state has made rainwater-harvesting structures compulsory in all houses, according to NCERT?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Tamil Nadu
Why: NCERT notes that Tamil Nadu has made rainwater-harvesting structures compulsory in every house.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the example NCERT gives.
Key point: Rainwater harvesting recharges groundwater and reduces runoff.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean. According to NCERT, how many lock systems does it have?
options: A) None, since it is a sea-level canal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Six
Why: NCERT notes that the Panama Canal, about 72 km long, has six lock systems, through which ships are lifted and lowered.
Why not the others: (A) describes the Suez Canal; (C) and (D) are not NCERT figures.
Key point: The canal cuts across the Isthmus of Panama between Panama City and Colon.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, commercial livestock rearing is organised on a scientific basis. What does it mainly emphasise?
options: A) Moving the herds from place to place in search of pasture
B) Breeding, genetic improvement, disease control and animal health
C) Rearing many kinds of animals together on small family plots
D) Using only wild animals caught from the forests
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Breeding, genetic improvement, disease control and animal health
Why: NCERT notes that ranching emphasises breeding, genetic improvement, disease control and the health care of animals.
Why not the others: (A) describes pastoral nomadism; (C) and (D) do not describe ranching.
Key point: Ranches usually rear only one type of animal.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Rural marketing centres
(B) Urban marketing centres
(C) Wholesale trading
(D) Quinary activities

List-II (Description in NCERT)
(I) Services of senior executives, government officials and research scientists
(II) Bulk business through intermediary merchants and supply houses
(III) Offer more widely specialised urban services
(IV) Quasi-urban centres serving nearby settlements with rudimentary trade
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: rural marketing centres are quasi-urban centres serving nearby settlements (IV); urban marketing centres offer more specialised services (III); wholesale trading is bulk business through intermediaries (II); quinary activities involve senior executives, officials and scientists (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the rural and urban centres; (C) swaps urban centres and wholesale trade; (D) swaps wholesale trade and quinary activities.
Key point: Periodic markets serve rural areas without regular markets.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Type of industry)
(A) Basic industries
(B) Consumer goods industries
(C) Joint sector industries
(D) Agro-processing

List-II (Description in NCERT)
(I) Turns farm produce into goods such as sugar, pickles and fruit juices
(II) Managed together by the public and private sectors
(III) Make goods consumed directly, such as bread, tea and soaps
(IV) Make products, such as iron and steel, used to make other goods
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: basic industries make products, such as iron and steel, used to make other goods (IV); consumer goods industries make goods consumed directly (III); joint sector industries are run by the public and private sectors together (II); agro-processing turns farm produce into finished goods (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps basic and consumer goods industries; (C) swaps consumer goods and joint sector; (D) swaps the joint sector and agro-processing.
Key point: Industries can be classified by size, raw material, output and ownership.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: To be a census town, a place needs a population of at least 5,000 and a density of at least 400 persons per sq km. What share of its male main workers must be in non-agricultural work?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) At least 75 per cent
Why: The Census of 2011 requires at least 75 per cent of the male main working population to be engaged in non-agricultural pursuits.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the Census threshold.
Key point: Statutory towns are those notified by law, such as municipalities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: In which year was air transport in India nationalised?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 1953
Why: NCERT notes that air transport in India was nationalised in 1953.
Why not the others: 1932 (A) is when air transport began in India; 1986 (C) is when the Inland Waterways Authority was set up; 1998 (D) is when the Konkan Railway was built.
Key point: Air transport is the fastest, but costliest, means of transport.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: Khasi and Santhali belong to which language family, according to NCERT?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Austric
Why: NCERT's table places Khasi (Mon-Khmer branch) and Santhali (Munda branch) in the Austro-Asiatic sub-family of the Austric family.
Why not the others: The Dravidian family (A) includes Tamil and Telugu; the Indo-European family (B) includes Hindi and Bengali; the Sino-Tibetan family (C) includes the Tibeto-Burman languages.
Key point: Austric languages are spoken in central and north-eastern India and the Nicobar Islands.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Human Development Index is based only on per capita income.
Reason (R): The HDI measures attainment in three areas: a long and healthy life, access to knowledge, and a decent standard of living.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
Why: The Assertion is false — income is only one of three dimensions. The Reason correctly gives the three areas the HDI measures.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) need a true Assertion.
Key point: The HDI was first published by the UNDP in 1990.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Griffith Taylor put forward the concept of neo-determinism, a middle path between environmental determinism and possibilism.
Reason (R): Neo-determinism is also known as "stop and go determinism".
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both statements are true, according to NCERT. But the other name of the concept does not explain why Taylor put it forward; the two are separate facts.
Why not the others: (A) treats the name as the cause; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Neo-determinism says humans can conquer nature by obeying it, heeding its "red signals".

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: According to NCERT, irrigation covers only about what share of India's cultivated area, leaving farming dependent on the monsoon?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) About 33 per cent
Why: NCERT notes that irrigation covers only about 33 per cent of the cultivated area, so most farming depends on the monsoon.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not NCERT figures.
Key point: Erratic monsoons cause both droughts and floods.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Example)
(A) The ravines of the Chambal
(B) Mining and industrial wastelands
(C) Urban smog
(D) Dharavi

List-II (Feature in NCERT)
(I) Asia's largest slum, in Mumbai
(II) A smoky fog over cities, caused by air pollution
(III) Land degraded by human activities
(IV) Gullied land formed by natural agents
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: the Chambal ravines are gullied land formed by natural agents (IV); mining and industrial wastelands are degraded by human activities (III); urban smog is a smoky fog caused by air pollution (II); Dharavi is Asia's largest slum (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the ravines and the wastelands; (B) swaps the wastelands and smog; (D) swaps smog and Dharavi.
Key point: Land degradation reduces the productivity of land.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: According to NCERT, Digboi and Barauni are examples of which types of oil refinery?
options: B) Digboi is market-based; Barauni is field-based
C) Digboi is field-based; Barauni is market-based
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Digboi is field-based; Barauni is market-based
Why: NCERT notes that refineries are either field-based, like Digboi, or market-based, like Barauni.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) are wrong; (B) swaps the two.
Key point: Market-based refineries are located near the consumers of petroleum products.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: According to NCERT, how are metropolitan cities and megacities defined?
options: A) Metropolitan: 1 to 5 million people; megacity: more than 5 million
B) Metropolitan: 1 to 10 lakh people; megacity: more than 10 lakh
C) Metropolitan: any state capital; megacity: any port city
D) Metropolitan: under 1 lakh people; megacity: 1 to 5 lakh
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Metropolitan: 1 to 5 million people; megacity: more than 5 million
Why: NCERT notes that cities with a population of one to five million are metropolitan cities, and those with more than five million are megacities.
Why not the others: (B) and (D) use the wrong thresholds; (C) uses function, not population.
Key point: Class I towns have a population of at least one lakh.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about tourist attractions, according to NCERT:
(A) Warm, sunny climates attract people from colder regions.
(B) Mountains, lakes and spectacular sea coasts draw many tourists.
(C) The history and art of a place attract visitors.
(D) Tourism has no link with the culture or economy of a place.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — NCERT lists culture and economy among tourist attractions, as with homestays and local cuisine. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Tourism supports infrastructure, retail trade and craft industries.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, which group forms the largest religious minority in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Muslims
Why: NCERT notes that Muslims are the largest religious minority, concentrated in Jammu and Kashmir, parts of West Bengal, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh, in and around Delhi, and in Lakshadweep.
Why not the others: Christians (A), Sikhs (B) and Buddhists (D) form smaller shares of the population.
Key point: Hindus form the largest religious group overall.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: In which states, according to NCERT, is the use of groundwater very high?
options: A) Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu
C) Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Nagaland
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu
Why: NCERT notes that groundwater use is very high in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu.
Why not the others: (B) is a group where use is relatively low; (C) and (D) are not the states named.
Key point: Over-use of groundwater lowers the water table.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: How has rice cultivation spread to drier areas such as Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh?
options: A) Through a sharp rise in rainfall over these areas
B) Through the clearing of forests in the Himalaya
C) Through imports of rice seeds from abroad only
D) Through canal irrigation and tube wells
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Through canal irrigation and tube wells
Why: NCERT notes that canal irrigation and tube wells have made it possible to grow rice in areas of lower rainfall, such as Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and northern Rajasthan.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the reasons NCERT gives.
Key point: Rice is grown under very different conditions across India.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
The Australian Trans-Continental Railway runs from Perth on the west coast to Sydney on the east coast. Arrange the following places on it from west to east:
(A) Broken Hill
(B) Kalgoorlie
(C) Sydney
(D) Port Augusta
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: From Perth the line runs east to Kalgoorlie (B), across the Nullarbor to Port Augusta (D), then to Broken Hill (A), and on to Sydney (C).
Why not the others: (A) puts Broken Hill before Port Augusta; (B) starts at Port Augusta; (C) puts Sydney before Broken Hill.
Key point: The railway crosses the southern part of the continent.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Consider the following statements, from NCERT's international comparisons of human development:
(A) The size of a territory is not directly related to its human development.
(B) Smaller countries have often done better than larger ones.
(C) Relatively poorer nations have sometimes been ranked higher than richer neighbours.
(D) Per capita income alone decides a country's HDI rank.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — the HDI also counts health and education, so income alone does not decide the rank. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: Sri Lanka ranks higher than India despite a smaller economy.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Every port serves an area, called its hinterland, from which it receives goods for export and to which it sends imported goods. India's ports differ in their sites and in the size of their hinterlands. Kolkata is an inland riverine port on the Hugli, about 128 km from the Bay of Bengal. Its hinterland covers much of the Ganga–Brahmaputra basin, but the river channel silts up, so Haldia was developed downstream to ease congestion. Mumbai has a spacious, well-sheltered natural harbour, and the Jawaharlal Nehru Port was built at Nhava Sheva as a satellite port to decongest it. Visakhapatnam is a landlocked harbour, linked to the sea by a channel cut through solid rock and sand. Chennai, one of the oldest ports on the east coast, has an artificial harbour built in 1859; it is not well suited to large ships because the water near the coast is shallow, and Ennore was built to its north to relieve the pressure on it.

Question: According to the passage, what is a port's hinterland?
options: A) The area that sends it exports and receives its imports
B) The stretch of open sea in front of the port's harbour
C) The group of ships that are registered at that port
D) The part of the port where cargo ships are repaired
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The area that sends it exports and receives its imports
Why: The passage defines the hinterland as the area a port serves — from which it receives goods for export and to which it sends imported goods.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are parts or features of a port, not the area it serves.
Key point: A rich and large hinterland makes a port important.

Question: Why was Haldia developed downstream of Kolkata?
options: A) Because Kolkata had no hinterland to serve
B) To export iron ore brought from distant Karnataka
C) To ease congestion, as Kolkata's river channel silts up
D) Because Kolkata stands directly on the open sea coast
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) To ease congestion, as Kolkata's river channel silts up
Why: The passage notes that the Hugli channel silts up, so Haldia was developed downstream to ease congestion at Kolkata.
Why not the others: (A) is false — Kolkata has a large hinterland; (B) relates to New Mangalore; (D) is false — Kolkata is about 128 km inland.
Key point: Silting forces regular dredging of the Hugli.

Question: Which port is described in the passage as a landlocked harbour, linked to the sea by a channel cut through solid rock and sand?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Visakhapatnam
Why: The passage describes Visakhapatnam as a landlocked harbour, connected to the sea by a channel cut through solid rock and sand.
Why not the others: Jawaharlal Nehru Port (A) is Mumbai's satellite port; Chennai (C) has an artificial harbour; Haldia (D) is a downstream port for Kolkata.

Question: Which statement about Chennai port is supported by the passage?
options: A) It is a natural harbour that was built only in recent years
B) It lies on a river, about 128 km inland from the open sea
C) It is the port best suited to the largest ships in India
D) An old artificial harbour, limited by shallow coastal water
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) An old artificial harbour, limited by shallow coastal water
Why: The passage notes that Chennai's artificial harbour was built in 1859 and is not well suited to large ships because the water near the coast is shallow.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) contradict the passage; (B) describes Kolkata.
Key point: Ennore was built to the north of Chennai to relieve the pressure on it.

Question: Kolkata, Mumbai and Chennai have each been given a new port nearby. What common reason does the passage suggest?
options: A) The old ports had lost all their hinterland to new ports
B) Each old port had congestion or limits that a new one could ease
C) The new ports were built only for passenger ships
D) The old ports had all been closed by the government
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Each old port had congestion or limits that a new one could ease
Why: Haldia eases congestion at Kolkata, the Jawaharlal Nehru Port decongests Mumbai, and Ennore relieves the pressure on Chennai — in each case a new port relieves an old one.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not supported by the passage.
Key point: Satellite and subsidiary ports share the traffic of busy old ports.
